target_customer: AI labs and robot makers that need independent evaluation of models controlling real robots
problem: There is no neutral, reproducible way to measure what frontier AI models can do when controlling physical robots.
business_model: Independent evaluations and benchmarks for labs, plus open source tooling; revenue model not stated
product_category: AI and robotics evaluation, public benefit corporation

founders.name: Jay Chooi
education: Harvard, MA Statistics and BA CS/Math
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. The launch post mentions a co-founder named Aris, not described on the page, so not listed as a founder.

competitors.name: Berkeley, Stanford and NVIDIA real robot evaluation platform
competitors.what: Crowdsourced real world network comparing robot policies

competitors.name: AGIBOT World Challenge 2026
competitors.what: Competition with online evaluation and real robot final

competitors.name: RoboBench
competitors.what: Benchmark of multimodal LLMs as embodied brain

technical_complexity.rationale: Building reproducible real robot harnesses and benchmarks needs hardware access and careful methodology, though the code framework is standard.

defensibility.rationale: Independence and trust, an open source framework with 97k to 112k installs, and accumulated results are hard to replicate, but benchmarks are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the role yet; labs have a conflict of interest evaluating themselves.

market_need_then: Physical AI models were multiplying in 2026 with mostly self reported results, creating demand for neutral measurement.

branding.domain_note: Uses robocurve.org, fitting a public benefit mission; no history found.

identity.visual_style: Curve motifs from score versus cost and time charts
identity.voice_and_tone: Measured, neutral and mission driven; reports results rigorously and independently.

branding.brand_signature: Open source Inspect Robots and the RoboDojo-RC benchmark names
branding.community_and_virality: Testimonials on the site from MATS, OpenAI, DeepMind and METR affiliated people; 112k+ PyPI installs claimed.

brand_strength.rationale: Coherent product family names and neutral voice, with developer adoption stated on the site, though independent brand press is thin.

outcome_analysis: Robocurve raised a $10M seed led by Initialized Capital in September 2026, shortly after its Summer 2026 batch, on the strength of a credible AI safety researcher founder and an open source framework with wide installs. It is early; the risk is monetizing a neutral evaluator and keeping independence from labs that pay.
notes: One aggregator also lists Pioneer Fund as an investor (not on other sources, omitted). Install counts vary (112k on the site, 97k in a news report). Incorporation date varies (June 24, 2026 on one profile). The YC launch post refers to co-founders Jay and Aris; only Jay Chooi has a full name in sources I opened. An aggregator wiki claims RoboDojo task details that I could not verify.
